learning_objective: 🎯 You will master the art of writing friendly letters to your family, and polite, official letters to your school principal or teachers!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Informal letters are chatty and relaxed! You write them to people you know well. You start with your address and date, write 'Dear [Name]', chat with them in the body, and end with 'Yours lovingly'.

Formal letters are serious and respectful. We write these to principals, editors, or companies. They have a strict format: Sender's address, Date, Receiver's address, Subject, 'Respected Sir/Madam', the body, and 'Yours obediently' or 'Yours sincerely'.

main_concepts.concept_title: 📌 The Power of the Subject Line
main_concepts.simple_explanation: In a formal letter, the 'Subject' is a one-line summary that tells the reader exactly why you are writing before they even read the full letter! For example: 'Subject: Application for two days sick leave.'

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Double Letter Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Write one polite sentence you would use to ask your Principal for a sports period (Formal), and one excited sentence you would use to tell your best friend about winning a game (Informal)!

quick_recap: ⭐ Informal letters are casual and written to friends and family.
⭐ Formal letters are respectful, follow a strict format, and are for officials like a Principal.
⭐ Formal letters always include the Receiver's Address and a short Subject line.
⭐ End informal letters with 'Yours lovingly' and formal letters with 'Yours obediently' or 'sincerely'.
